origen_duracion: Fuente. [LeRoux-2C] p. PDF 4, impresa 4: «Moreover, during the initial seedling stage, low daily average temperatures below 2 °C (during more than 2 successive days) delay emergence and induce poor vigor plantlets33.»

tipo_umbral: según días desde el encañado (−4,2 a 0 °C, Feng et al. 1999)
umbral_texto: Tmin ≤ −4.2 / −3.5 / −2.5 / −1.0 / 0 °C según días desde el encañado
definicion_evento: Cada día con Tmin bajo el umbral del día (según los días desde el encañado) es un evento (1 día basta). Una clase: helada grave.
origen_duracion: Fuente. El dato es la Tmin del día en que ocurrió la helada: [Feng-datos] p. PDF 2, impresa 336: «霜冻害发生日的最低气温、当年的拔节期，霜冻害程度等取自河南、安徽、山东、山西、江苏、陕西等省 51 个农业气象基本观测站 1981～1997 年共 17 年的资料。» Umbral y clase: [Feng-umbral] p. PDF 4, impresa 338: «研究小麦霜冻害最好用植株体温，但是气象站不进行这种观测。可供分析的完整资料是最低气温。历史资料表明，同一时段发生重霜冻害的最低气温有高有低，以其中的最高值作为指标，可以得出：拔节期到拔节前 4 天为－4.2℃，拔节后 1～5 天为－3.5℃，6～10 天为－2.5℃，11～15 天为－1.0℃，16～20 天为 0℃。这个指标与陶祖文的研究结果[4]相近。需要指出的是，在各个时段里都有许多日期的最低气温低于上述指标，但是并没有发生重霜冻害，而只发生轻霜冻害。这是因为最低气温与最低叶温之间没有一一对应的函数关系。» (PDF escaneado: transcripción cotejada visualmente).
fuente: Feng, Y. (冯玉香); He, W.; Sun, Z.; Zhong, X. (1999). 我国冬小麦霜冻害的气候分析 [Climatological study on frost damage of winter wheat in China]. 作物学报 (Acta Agronomica Sinica) 25(3), 335–340. Sin DOI

definicion_evento: Cada día con Tmin < 0 °C es un evento (1 día basta). Severidad del modelo: multiplicador de rendimiento 0,1 por día con helada en Z49–Z80.
origen_duracion: Fuente. [Zheng-umbral] p. PDF 3, impresa 3613: «To approximate the distributions of exposed heads at susceptible post-heading stages, a multiplier was applied from 1 (i.e. no yield loss) at the late-booting average stage (Z45) followed by a linear decrease to 0.1 (i.e. 90% yield loss) against Zadoks score up to mid-heading (Z55), when almost all tillers would have reached the susceptible post-heading stage (Z49). Maximum susceptibility (i.e. all tillers susceptible) was then maintained until the start of dough development (Z80), with a constant yield multiplier of 0.1 (i.e. 90% yield loss) over the developmental period Z49–Z80 for each day with a minimum temperature below a threshold of 0 °C. After Z80, the yield multiplier was linearly increased over time (from 0.1 to 1) up to the completion of dough development (Z89), which reflected late frost events causing cessation of grain development.»
fuente: Zheng, B.; Chapman, S. C.; Christopher, J. T.; Frederiks, T. M.; Chenu, K. (2015). Frost trends and their estimated impact on yield in the Australian wheatbelt. Journal of Experimental Botany 66(12), 3611–3623. DOI 10.1093/jxb/erv163 (acceso abierto)

definicion_evento: Racha de 2 días consecutivos con P ≥ 25 mm cada día (una vez por racha). Sin grados.
origen_duracion: Fuente (tratamiento experimental). [Ellis-dosis] p. PDF 2–3, impresa 68–69: «The rainfall simulation was the equivalent of 25 mm rainfall, with two treatments applied late in seed maturation. Control plants were harvested at 55 (10 August), 56 (11 August) or 62 DAA (17 August). Wetting 1 was at 56 DAA, with seeds harvested 30 min after wetting (nominally 56.02 DAA) and 6 d later (62 DAA). The second treatment comprised two simulated rainfall events 1 d apart, each of 25 mm, [salto de pág. 68→69] at 55 and 56 DAA.»
fuente: Ellis, R. H.; Yadav, G. (2016). Effect of simulated rainfall during wheat seed development and maturation on subsequent seed longevity is reversible. Seed Science Research 26, 67–76. DOI 10.1017/S0960258515000392

definicion_evento: Cada día con Tmin < 0 °C es un evento (1 día basta). Grado por intensidad según la fuente: daño leve bajo 0 °C; mayor bajo −2 °C (p. 4; la fuente no da cifra para «prolonged periods»).
origen_duracion: Fuente. [Mourtzinis-tmin] p. PDF 4, impresa 4: «Using the 21 days earlier sowing as a threshold, 2% of all 289 locations (all in North Dakota, South Dakota, and Minnesota) exceeded the 20% probability threshold for daily minimum temperatures to drop below 0 °C at emergence and only 0.3% had exceeded the 20% probability for daily minimum temperatures to drop below −1 °C (Fig. 4).» Intensidad: [Mourtzinis-dano] p. PDF 4, impresa 4: «An important consideration in early sowing is spring frost occurrence, which can damage or destroy the crop (but only after emergence at 15–25 DAS)16. The current common recommendation to soybean producers is to sow the first field when frost probabilities are less than 20% on or after emergence. Minor frost damage on emerged seedlings may occur when temperature drops below 0 °C, but becomes more damaging when tempera-ture drops below −2 °C for prolonged periods.»
fuente: Mourtzinis, S.; Specht, J. E.; Conley, S. P. (2019). Scientific Reports 9, 2800. DOI 10.1038/s41598-019-38971-3

definicion_evento: Cada día con Teff > 35 °C dentro de la TSP es un evento (1 día basta). Grado por intensidad según la fuente: factor diario lineal entre Tcr = 35 °C y Tlim = 40 °C (ec. A.6); daño máximo con Teff ≥ 40 °C.
origen_duracion: Fuente. [Deryng-tsp] p. PDF 11, impresa 10: «Crop TSP includes a couple of days before and after anthesis and is estimated as a function of crop growing period length (GPL), which depends on growing degree days accumulation [5] and varies with crop cultivars. Anthesis is scheduled when the number of days since emergence reaches half of crop GPL (calculated between emergence and maturity), i.e., 0.5 GPL; TSP starts a few days before anthesis at 0.45 GPL and ends after anthesis at 0.7 GPL. A high temperature event occurs when daily effective temperature (Teff) exceeds a critical temperature (Tcr) threshold.» [Deryng-teff] p. PDF 11, impresa 10: «Teff is defined as (Tmean + Tmax)/2, where Tmean is the daily mean temperature and Tmax is the daily maximum tempera-ture [44], Tlim is the limit temperature above which fHSAd is maximal. Crop specific Tcr and Tlim come from a synthesis of values found in the literature [10, 11, 14, 33, 45–49] (table A.1). Temperature tolerance differs for each crop. Here, HSA critical temperature thresholds are 25 ◦C for spring wheat, 32 ◦C for maize and 35 ◦C for soybean. Hence, as temperatures increase spring wheat yield is impacted first, followed by maize and finally soybean. However, HSA impact functions differ among crop type as temperature thresholds at zero pod-set are 35 ◦C for spring wheat, 45 ◦C for maize and 40 ◦C for soybean.»
fuente: Deryng, D.; Conway, D.; Ramankutty, N.; Price, J.; Warren, R. (2014). Global crop yield response to extreme heat stress under multiple climate change futures. Environmental Research Letters 9, 034011. DOI 10.1088/1748-9326/9/3/034011

definicion_evento: Evento = la condición se cumple en la ventana (0/1 por temporada). Condición: media de la Tmax diaria de la fase > 30 °C.
origen_duracion: No es racha: promedio de fase. [Hoffman-fases] p. PDF 3, impresa 2: «For each climate variable in table 1, we computed four predictors based on phenological phases defined as establishment, critical window, and grain filling, and averages for the entire cycle from planting to maturity.» [Hoffman-gf] p. PDF 9, impresa 8: «Modeled yield responses of maize and soybean yields to TMAX-GF compare favorably to those found in other work wherein yields increase slowly with increasing temperature until a threshold and then fall off rapidly (Schlenker and Roberts 2009, Lobell et al 2014). definicion_evento: Evento = la condición se cumple en la ventana (0/1 por temporada). Condición: lluvia acumulada en R6–R8 > 100 mm. Una sola ventana compartida por FIL y MAT: contar una vez.
origen_duracion: No es racha: total de ventana. [Weer-100mm] p. PDF 16, impresa 16 of 19: «Maternal environmental conditions at the late reproductive stage (R6–R8) are the most critical factor in determining the initial seed quality. Rapid seed deterioration in the field occurred when more than 100 mm of cumulative rainfall coincided with the late reproductive stage.» [Weer-fases] p. PDF 5, impresa 5 of 19: «To understand the influence of production environment, the total growing period (TGP) was partitioned into three stages; (i) seed sowing (SS) to flowering (R1) as vegetative (VEG), (ii) flowering to full seed stage (R6) as early reproductive (ER), and (iii) full seed stage to full mature stage (R8) as late reproductive stage (LR).»
fuente: Weerasekara, I.; Sinniah, U. R.; et al. (2021). The Influence of Seed Production Environment on Seed Development and Quality of Soybean. Agronomy 11(7), 1430. DOI 10.3390/agronomy11071430
